studies.title: Microtubule associated protein 2 in bipolar depression: Impact of pregnenolone.
studies.abstract: Pregnenolone, and related neurosteroids, may have antidepressant properties. Preclinical research proposes that microtubule associated protein 2 (MAP2) binding may be a mechanism for antidepressant properties of pregnenolone. Thus, MAP2 might be a novel target for antidepressant therapy. This clinical study is the first to examine serum MAP2 levels in people with bipolar depression and controls, and whether pregnenolone treatment is associated with a change in MAP2 levels. Blood samples from a previously published clinical trial of pregnenolone for adult bipolar depression were analyzed at baseline and week 6 of treatment with pregnenolone or placebo for serum MAP2 levels using Western Blot. MAP2 levels from healthy controls were also obtained. MAP2 levels in the bipolar depressed patients (n=11) tended to be higher than in controls (n=4) (p=0.062). MAP2 levels decreased non-significantly from baseline to week 6 in placebo (n=5) and pregnenolone-treated patients (n=6). MAP2 level changes correlated positively with change in self-reported depressive symptom scores in the pregnenolone group (r=0.771, p=0.072) but not in the placebo group (r=0.000, p=1.000). This study, exploring relationships between MAP-2 in humans with mood disorders, is limited by the small sample size. Thus, the findings must be viewed with great caution. These findings suggest possible differences in serum MAP-2 levels between bipolar depressed persons and controls and a relationship between changes in depressive symptoms and MAP-2 levels during pregnenolone therapy. Findings suggest additional research is needed on MAP-2 in mood disorders.

studies.title: Pregnenolone as an adjunct to risperidone for treatment of women with schizophrenia: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial.
studies.abstract: There have been few studies of pregnenolone therapy in schizophrenia and those that exist have been subject to several critical limitations, thus yielding inconsistent results. We attempted to assess the therapeutic effect of pregnenolone in a patient sample as homogeneous as possible. In this randomized double-blind clinical trial, 82 female inpatients with chronic schizophrenia, who had discontinued their antipsychotic medications for at least one week in case of any oral antipsychotic medication or a month for any depot antipsychotic medication, received risperidone plus either pregnenolone (50 mg/day) or placebo for 8 weeks. Inclusion criteria were acute illness with a baseline Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) negative subscale score of ≥20. Exclusion criteria were the presence of severe depression or other concomitant psychiatric disorders. Primary outcome was defined as the difference in the PANSS total score change from baseline to week 8 in the pregnenolone group compared to the placebo group. No significant difference was found in the PANSS total score changes between the two arms (mean difference (CI 95%) = -9.41 (-20.24 to 1.41); p = 0.087). Significant differences were initially found for PANSS negative change scores (mean difference (CI 95%) = -2.61 (-5.03 to -0.19); p = 0.035) and general psychopathology change scores (mean difference (CI 95%) = -5.93 (-11.37 to -0.48); p = 0.033). However, these findings did not survive Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. While this trial may suggest a potential effect of pregnenolone on schizophrenia symptoms, further studies are warranted.

studies.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of pregnenolone for bipolar depression.
studies.abstract: Depression in bipolar disorder (BPD) is challenging to treat. Therefore, additional medication options are needed. In the current report, the effect of the neurosteroid pregnenolone on depressive symptoms in BPD was examined. Adults (n=80) with BPD, depressed mood state, were randomized to pregnenolone (titrated to 500 mg/day) or placebo, as add-on therapy, for 12 weeks. Outcome measures included the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD), Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology-Self-Report (IDS-SR), Hamilton Rating Scale for Anxiety (HRSA), and Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS). Serum neurosteroid levels were assessed at baseline and week 12. Data were analyzed using a mixed model ANCOVA with a between factor of treatment assignment, a within factor (repeated) of visit, and the baseline value, as well as age and gender, as covariates. In participants with at least one postbaseline visit (n=73), a significant treatment by week interaction for the HRSD (F(5,288)=2.61, p=0.025), but not IDS-SR, was observed. Depression remission rates were greater in the pregnenolone group (61%) compared with the placebo group (37%), as assessed by the IDS-SR (χ(2)(1)=3.99, p=0.046), but not the HRSD. Large baseline-to-exit changes in neurosteroid levels were observed in the pregnenolone group but not in the placebo group. In the pregnenolone group, baseline-to-exit change in the HRSA correlated negatively with changes in allopregnanolone (r(22)=-0.43, p=0.036) and pregNANolone (r(22)=-0.48, p=0.019) levels. Pregnenolone was well tolerated. The results suggest that pregnenolone may improve depressive symptoms in patients with BPD and can be safely administered.

studies.title: Proof-of-concept randomized controlled trial of pregnenolone in schizophrenia.
studies.abstract: Preclinical and clinical data suggest that pregnenolone may be a promising therapeutic in schizophrenia. Pregnenolone is neuroprotective and enhances learning and memory, myelination, and microtubule polymerization. Treatment with pregnenolone elevates allopregnanolone (a neurosteroid that enhances GABAA receptor responses) and pregnenolone sulfate (a positive NMDA receptor modulator). Pregnenolone could thus potentially mitigate GABA dysregulation and/or NMDA receptor hypofunction in schizophrenia via metabolism to other neurosteroids. The objective of this study is to conduct a randomized controlled trial of adjunctive pregnenolone in schizophrenia. Following a placebo lead-in, 120 participants were randomized to pregnenolone or placebo for 8 weeks (Institute for Mental Health, Singapore). Primary endpoints were changes in MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery (MCCB) composite scores (cognitive symptoms), UCSD Performance-based Skills Assessment-Brief (UPSA-B) composite scores (functional capacity), and Scale for Assessment of Negative Symptoms (SANS) total scores (negative symptoms). A modified intent-to-treat analysis approach was utilized. No significant changes compared to placebo were demonstrated in composite MCCB scores. In contrast, participants randomized to pregnenolone (n = 56) demonstrated greater improvements in functional capacity (UPSA-B composite changes) compared to placebo (n = 55), p = 0.03. Pregnenolone was also superior to placebo in the communication subscale of the UPSA-B (p < 0.001). Serum pregnenolone changes post-treatment were correlated with UPSA-B composite score changes in females (r s = 0.497, p < 0.042, n = 17) but not in males. Mean total SANS scores were very low at baseline and did not improve further post-treatment. Pregnenolone was well-tolerated. Pregnenolone improved functional capacity in participants with schizophrenia, but did not improve cognitive symptoms over an 8-week treatment period. Neurosteroid changes correlated with functional improvements in female participants. Neurosteroid interventions may exhibit promise as new therapeutic leads for schizophrenia.

studies.title: Proof-of-concept trial with the neurosteroid pregnenolone targeting cognitive and negative symptoms in schizophrenia.
studies.abstract: The neurosteroid pregnenolone and its sulfated derivative enhance learning and memory in rodents. Pregnenolone sulfate also positively modulates NMDA receptors and could thus ameliorate hypothesized NMDA receptor hypofunction in schizophrenia. Furthermore, clozapine increases pregnenolone in rodent hippocampus, possibly contributing to its superior efficacy. We therefore investigated adjunctive pregnenolone for cognitive and negative symptoms in patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder receiving stable doses of second-generation antipsychotics in a pilot randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial. Following a 2-week single-blind placebo lead-in, patients were randomized to pregnenolone (fixed escalating doses to 500 mg/day) or placebo, for 8 weeks. Primary end points were changes in BACS and MCCB composite and total SANS scores. Of 21 patients randomized, 18 completed at least 4 weeks of treatment (n=9/group). Pregnenolone was well tolerated. Patients receiving pregnenolone demonstrated significantly greater improvements in SANS scores (mean change=10.38) compared with patients receiving placebo (mean change=2.33), p=0.048. Mean composite changes in BACS and MCCB scores were not significantly different in patients randomized to pregnenolone compared with placebo. However, serum pregnenolone increases predicted BACS composite scores at 8 weeks in the pregnenolone group (r(s)=0.81, p=0.022). Increases in allopregnanolone, a GABAergic pregnenolone metabolite, also predicted BACS composite scores (r(s)=0.74, p=0.046). In addition, baseline pregnenolone (r(s)=-0.76, p=0.037), pregnenolone sulfate (r(s)=-0.83, p=0.015), and allopregnanolone levels (r(s)=-0.83, p=0.015) were inversely correlated with improvements in MCCB composite scores, further supporting a possible role for neurosteroids in cognition. Mean BACS and MCCB composite scores were correlated (r(s)=0.74, p<0.0001). Pregnenolone may be a promising therapeutic agent for negative symptoms and merits further investigation for cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia.

studies.title: Pregnenolone reduces provoked craving and cocaine use in men and women with cocaine use disorder: A pilot trial.
studies.abstract: Chronic cocaine use decreases neuroactive steroid (NAS) levels, contributing to continued cocaine use and high risk of return to use in individuals with cocaine use disorder (CUD). This pilot study assessed chronic treatment with two doses of the NAS precursor pregnenolone to boost endogenous NAS levels and affect provoked craving and cocaine use outcomes in an 8-week trial in men and women with CUD. Fifty-five treatment-seeking individuals with CUD were randomly assigned to receive either placebo (PLA; n = 18; 12M/6F), 300mg PREG/day (n = 20; 15M/5F) or 500mg PREG/day (n = 17; 12M/5F) for 8 weeks. Plasma collected at weeks 2, 5 and 7 was assessed for pregnenolone levels. A subset participated in a 3-day experimental component of guided imagery exposure to stress, cocaine and neutral cues in about week 2 of the trial to assess craving response. Cocaine use outcomes were assessed during the treatment period. Intent-to-treat analyses were conducted using linear mixed effects models. Pregnenolone levels were higher in the 300mg and 500mg PREG groups compared to PLA (p's < 0.032). Stress (p < .001) and cocaine cue (p < .001) induced craving increased in PLA, but not in PREG groups. 300mg PREG used lower cocaine amounts compared to 500mg PREG group (p = 0.01) and PLA (p = .047). A non-significant reduction was observed for % days of cocaine used (p = .122). These pilot findings suggest that PREG reduces cocaine craving and improves cocaine use outcomes in treatment seeking individuals with CUD, supporting further assessment of PREG in the treatment of CUD.

studies.title: Pregnenolone effects on provoked alcohol craving, anxiety, HPA axis, and autonomic arousal in individuals with alcohol use disorder.
studies.abstract: Chronic alcohol intake down-regulates GABAergic transmission and reduces levels of neuroactive steroids. These changes are associated with greater stress dysregulation and high alcohol craving which in turn increases relapse risk. This study tested whether potentiation of the neurosteroid system with pregnenolone (PREG), a precursor to neuroactive steroids and known to increase GABAergic transmission, will normalize chronic alcohol-related stress adaptations in the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic responses and reduce alcohol craving to significantly impact relapse risk. Forty-three treatment-seeking individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD) were randomized to placebo (PBO) or supraphysiologic pregnenolone doses of 300 mg or 500 mg treatment using a parallel-between subject design as part of a larger 8-week pilot clinical trial. In week 2, they participated in a 3-day laboratory experiment where on each day they self-administered the assigned study drug in the laboratory and were then exposed to 5-min personalized guided imagery provocation of stress, alcohol, or neutral/relaxing cues, one condition per day on separate days, in a random, counterbalanced order. Repeated assessments of alcohol craving, anxiety, HPA axis, heart rate (HR), systolic (SBP), and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and serum pregnenolone levels were made on each day. Pregnenolone levels were significantly increased in the PREG groups versus PBO. PREG treatment decreased stress- and alcohol cue- induced craving and dose-specifically reduced stress-induced anxiety in the 300 mg/day group. Both PREG doses compared to PBO also normalized CORT/ACTH and increased stress-induced HR, stress- and cue-induced SBP, and in the 300 mg PREG group cue-induced DBP responses relative to neutral condition. Findings indicate that pregnenolone decreases stress- and alcohol cue-provoked craving and normalizes HPA axis and autonomic arousal in individuals with AUD, thereby supporting the need for further assessment of pregnenolone in the treatment of AUD.

studies.title: Pregnenolone Reduces Stress-Induced Craving, Anxiety, and Autonomic Arousal in Individuals with Cocaine Use Disorder.
studies.abstract: Chronic cocaine use leads to adaptations in stress biology and in neuroactive steroid system. These adaptations are associated with high cocaine craving and increased relapse risk. This study tested whether potentiation of the neuroactive steroid system with the precursor pregnenolone (PREG) affects stress- and cue-induced cocaine craving, anxiety and autonomic response in individuals with cocaine use disorder (CUD). Thirty treatment-seeking individuals (21 Male, 9 Female) with CUD were randomized to placebo (PBO) or supraphysiologic PREG doses of 300 mg or 500 mg per day for 8 weeks. After 2 weeks of treatment, participants were exposed to 5-min personalized guided imagery provocation of stress, cocaine, or neutral/relaxing cues in a 3-day experiment, one condition per day on separate days, in a random, counterbalanced order. Repeated assessment of cocaine craving, anxiety, heart rate (HR), systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were assessed on each day. PREG significantly increased pregnenolone levels compared to PBO. Both PREG doses decreased stress- and cocaine cue-induced craving and reduced both stress- and cue-induced anxiety only in the 500 mg/day group. The 500 mg/day PREG group also displayed decreased stress-induced HR, SBP and DBP. Findings indicate that pregnenolone decreases stress- and cocaine cue-provoked craving and anxiety and reduces stress-induced autonomic arousal in individuals with CUD.

studies.title: The neurosteroids allopregnanolone and dehydroepiandrosterone modulate resting-state amygdala connectivity.
studies.abstract: The neurosteroids allopregnanolone and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) are integral components of the stress response and exert positive modulatory effects on emotion in both human and animal studies. Although these antidepressant and anxiolytic effects have been well established, to date, little research has examined their neural correlates, and no research has been conducted into the effects of neurosteroids on large-scale networks at rest. To investigate the neurosteroid impact on intrinsic connectivity networks, participants were administered 400 mg of pregnenolone (N = 16), 400 mg of DHEA (N = 14), or placebo (N = 15) and underwent 3T fMRI. Resting-state brain connectivity was measured using amygdala as a seed region. When compared with placebo, pregnenolone administration reduced connectivity between amygdala and dorsal medial prefrontal cortex, between amygdala and precuneus, and between amygdala and hippocampus. DHEA reduced connectivity between amygdala and periamygdala and between amygdala and insula. Reductions in amygdala to precuneus connectivity were associated with less self-reported negative affect. These results demonstrate that neurosteroids modulate amygdala functional connectivity during resting state and may be a target for pharmacological intervention. Additionally, allopregnanolone and DHEA may shift the balance between salience network and default network, a finding that could provide insight into the neurocircuitry of anxiety psychopathology.

studies.title: Stability and Reliability of Repeated Plasma Pregnenolone Levels After Oral Pregnenolone Dosing in Individuals with Cocaine Use Disorder: Pilot Findings.
studies.abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs), including cocaine use disorder (CUD), have significant negative health risks and impose a substantial social burden, yet effective treatments are limited. Pregnenolone, a neuroactive steroid precursor, has been shown to reduce alcohol craving and normalize stress biology in individuals with CUD, but its clinical utility has been questioned due to limited data on bioavailability and the stability of blood levels in humans. Thus, this pilot study aimed to determine whether twice-daily oral pregnenolone (PREG) at 300 mg/day and 500 mg/day versus placebo in week two of PREG administration led to stable increased plasma pregnenolone levels in individuals with CUD. Seven treatment-seeking individuals with CUD, enrolled in an eight-week double-blind clinical trial, were randomized to receive placebo (n = 2) or pregnenolone at 300 mg/day (n = 3) or 500 mg/day (n = 2). For the first two weeks of the eight-week trial, participants were admitted to an inpatient Clinical Neuroscience Research Unit for repeated serial sampling of plasma pregnenolone concentrations over a 32.5 h period in week two of their inpatient stay while taking their assigned study drug under observation. Pregnenolone levels showed a significant main effect of the medication group (p = 0.039), with sustained higher levels in the 300 mg (p = 0.018) and 500 mg (p = 0.035) groups compared to placebo, and no significant difference between the two pregnenolone dosing groups. Moreover, correlation analyses showed that after observed study medication dosing on repeated sampling day 1, levels of pregnenolone were highly associated across time, with strong, positive correlations between time of dosing and 2 h (r = 0.80, p = 0.031), 4 h (r = 0.80, p = 0.031), 6 h (r = 0.86, p = 0.013), and 8 h post-dosing (r = 0.97, p < 0.001). These findings from this pilot study suggest that chronic twice-daily/"bis in die" (b.i.d.) oral administration of pregnenolone at both 300 mg/day and 500 mg/day achieved stable and reliable elevated plasma pregnenolone levels over 32.5 h in individuals with CUD, thereby supporting the good bioavailability of pregnenolone in these samples. These data indicate that twice-daily chronic dosing may overcome any potential concerns of poor bioavailability and rapid metabolism of pregnenolone in humans, and support further clinical investigations into pregnenolone's role in the treatment of cocaine use disorders.

studies.title: Pregnenolone sulfate induces transcriptional and immunoregulatory effects on T cells.
studies.abstract: Pregnenolone sulfate is a steroid metabolite of the steroidogenesis precursor, pregnenolone, with similar functional properties, including immunosuppression. We recently reported an elevation in serum levels of pregnenolone sulfate in children with malaria, contributing to an immunosuppressed state. Yet, the molecular mechanisms in which this steroid exerts its immunoregulatory functions are lacking. In this study, we examined the effects of pregnenolone sulfate on T cell viability, proliferation and transcriptome. We observed a pregnenolone sulfate dose-dependent induction of T cell death and reduction in proliferation. RNA sequencing analysis of pregnenolone sulfate-treated T cells for 2 and 24 h revealed the downregulation of pro-inflammatory genes and the upregulation of the steroid nuclear receptor superfamily, NR4A, as early-response genes. We also report a strong activation of the integrated stress response mediated by the upregulation of EIF2AK3. These results contribute to the knowledge on transcriptional regulation driving the immunoregulatory effects of pregnenolone sulfate on T cells.

studies.title: Placebo Effect in Clinical Trials in Autism: Experience from a Pregnenolone Treatment Study.
studies.abstract:
Purpose

The placebo effect is a significant limitation in subjective report, particularly when using informant-based outcome measures. In autism spectrum disorder (ASD), this effect is particularly complex due to high expectations for positive treatment outcomes. Therefore, interventional research in ASD needs to account for and remediate the placebo response.

Methods

This preliminary pilot report examines placebo effect in a single-blind, two-week placebo lead-in that preceded the double-blind phase of a randomized controlled trial. The trial assessed pregnenolone, an endogenous neurosteroid, for reducing irritability in adolescents and young adults (ages 14-25) with ASD. The Aberrant Behaviors Checklist (ABC) irritability subscale (ABC-I) was the primary outcome measure used to identify correlates of the placebo effect (IQ, age, sex, and baseline symptom severity). Paired, 2-tailed t-tests compared outcome measures at baseline and following the lead-in.

Results

Twenty-five participants (23 males, 2 females; mean age 18.5 ± 3.1 years) have completed the trial to date. The two-week lead-in resulted in a 30.2% decrease in irritability symptoms (t(24) = 5.090(24), p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.018) across all participants. The remaining ABC subscales also decreased significantly. The magnitude of change in ABC-I was correlated (rs=0.488, p = 0.013) with baseline ABC-I score, but not sex, IQ, or age.

Conclusion

Findings from this preliminary pilot trial provide evidence of a significant placebo effect in a clinical trial for ASD, further highlighting the challenges that this phenomenon presents for interventional research. A single-blind placebo lead-in within ASD clinical trials is a recommended approach to both account and mitigate for the placebo effect.

studies.title: Does Pregnenolone Adjunct to Risperidone Ameliorate Irritable Behavior in Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Control
studies.abstract: Pregnenolone is a neurosteroid with modulatory effects on γ-aminobutyric acid neurotransmission. Here, we aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of pregnenolone add-on to risperidone in adolescents with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Sixty-four ASD patients were randomly allocated to receive either pregnenolone (n = 32) or matching placebo (n = 32) in addition to risperidone. The Aberrant Behavior Checklist-Community Edition scale was used to evaluate the behavioral status of patients at baseline, week 5, and the trial end point. The change in score of irritability subscale was the primary outcome. Frequency of adverse effects due to trial medications was compared between the treatment groups. Fifty-nine patients completed the trial (30 in pregnenolone and 29 in the placebo arm). Baseline characteristics of both treatment groups were similar (P > 0.05). Repeated measures analysis was suggestive of greater exhibited improvement for the pregnenolone group on irritability, stereotypy, and hyperactivity subscales of the Aberrant Behavior Checklist-Community Edition over the trial period (F = 3.84, df = 1.96, P = 0.025; F = 4.29, df = 1.39, P = 0.029; F = 6.55, df = 1.67, P = 0.004, respectively). Nonetheless, the alterations in lethargy and inappropriate speech domains scores were similar for both arms (F = 0.93, df = 1.49, P = 0.375; F = 1.10, df = 1.60, P = 0.325, respectively). There was no significant difference in frequency as well as severity of adverse effects between the 2 groups. Pregnenolone adjunct to risperidone could attenuate core features associated with ASD.

studies.title: Microtubule associated protein 2 in bipolar depression: Impact of pregnenolone.
studies.abstract: Pregnenolone, and related neurosteroids, may have antidepressant properties. Preclinical research proposes that microtubule associated protein 2 (MAP2) binding may be a mechanism for antidepressant properties of pregnenolone. Thus, MAP2 might be a novel target for antidepressant therapy. This clinical study is the first to examine serum MAP2 levels in people with bipolar depression and controls, and whether pregnenolone treatment is associated with a change in MAP2 levels. Blood samples from a previously published clinical trial of pregnenolone for adult bipolar depression were analyzed at baseline and week 6 of treatment with pregnenolone or placebo for serum MAP2 levels using Western Blot. MAP2 levels from healthy controls were also obtained. MAP2 levels in the bipolar depressed patients (n=11) tended to be higher than in controls (n=4) (p=0.062). MAP2 levels decreased non-significantly from baseline to week 6 in placebo (n=5) and pregnenolone-treated patients (n=6). MAP2 level changes correlated positively with change in self-reported depressive symptom scores in the pregnenolone group (r=0.771, p=0.072) but not in the placebo group (r=0.000, p=1.000). This study, exploring relationships between MAP-2 in humans with mood disorders, is limited by the small sample size. Thus, the findings must be viewed with great caution. These findings suggest possible differences in serum MAP-2 levels between bipolar depressed persons and controls and a relationship between changes in depressive symptoms and MAP-2 levels during pregnenolone therapy. Findings suggest additional research is needed on MAP-2 in mood disorders.

studies.title: Pregnenolone as an adjunct to risperidone for treatment of women with schizophrenia: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial.
studies.abstract: There have been few studies of pregnenolone therapy in schizophrenia and those that exist have been subject to several critical limitations, thus yielding inconsistent results. We attempted to assess the therapeutic effect of pregnenolone in a patient sample as homogeneous as possible. In this randomized double-blind clinical trial, 82 female inpatients with chronic schizophrenia, who had discontinued their antipsychotic medications for at least one week in case of any oral antipsychotic medication or a month for any depot antipsychotic medication, received risperidone plus either pregnenolone (50 mg/day) or placebo for 8 weeks. Inclusion criteria were acute illness with a baseline Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) negative subscale score of ≥20. Exclusion criteria were the presence of severe depression or other concomitant psychiatric disorders. Primary outcome was defined as the difference in the PANSS total score change from baseline to week 8 in the pregnenolone group compared to the placebo group. No significant difference was found in the PANSS total score changes between the two arms (mean difference (CI 95%) = -9.41 (-20.24 to 1.41); p = 0.087). Significant differences were initially found for PANSS negative change scores (mean difference (CI 95%) = -2.61 (-5.03 to -0.19); p = 0.035) and general psychopathology change scores (mean difference (CI 95%) = -5.93 (-11.37 to -0.48); p = 0.033). However, these findings did not survive Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. While this trial may suggest a potential effect of pregnenolone on schizophrenia symptoms, further studies are warranted.

studies.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of pregnenolone for bipolar depression.
studies.abstract: Depression in bipolar disorder (BPD) is challenging to treat. Therefore, additional medication options are needed. In the current report, the effect of the neurosteroid pregnenolone on depressive symptoms in BPD was examined. Adults (n=80) with BPD, depressed mood state, were randomized to pregnenolone (titrated to 500 mg/day) or placebo, as add-on therapy, for 12 weeks. Outcome measures included the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD), Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology-Self-Report (IDS-SR), Hamilton Rating Scale for Anxiety (HRSA), and Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS). Serum neurosteroid levels were assessed at baseline and week 12. Data were analyzed using a mixed model ANCOVA with a between factor of treatment assignment, a within factor (repeated) of visit, and the baseline value, as well as age and gender, as covariates. In participants with at least one postbaseline visit (n=73), a significant treatment by week interaction for the HRSD (F(5,288)=2.61, p=0.025), but not IDS-SR, was observed. Depression remission rates were greater in the pregnenolone group (61%) compared with the placebo group (37%), as assessed by the IDS-SR (χ(2)(1)=3.99, p=0.046), but not the HRSD. Large baseline-to-exit changes in neurosteroid levels were observed in the pregnenolone group but not in the placebo group. In the pregnenolone group, baseline-to-exit change in the HRSA correlated negatively with changes in allopregnanolone (r(22)=-0.43, p=0.036) and pregNANolone (r(22)=-0.48, p=0.019) levels. Pregnenolone was well tolerated. The results suggest that pregnenolone may improve depressive symptoms in patients with BPD and can be safely administered.
studies.journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology

studies.title: Proof-of-concept trial with the neurosteroid pregnenolone targeting cognitive and negative symptoms in schizophrenia.
studies.abstract: The neurosteroid pregnenolone and its sulfated derivative enhance learning and memory in rodents. Pregnenolone sulfate also positively modulates NMDA receptors and could thus ameliorate hypothesized NMDA receptor hypofunction in schizophrenia. Furthermore, clozapine increases pregnenolone in rodent hippocampus, possibly contributing to its superior efficacy. We therefore investigated adjunctive pregnenolone for cognitive and negative symptoms in patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder receiving stable doses of second-generation antipsychotics in a pilot randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial. Following a 2-week single-blind placebo lead-in, patients were randomized to pregnenolone (fixed escalating doses to 500 mg/day) or placebo, for 8 weeks. Primary end points were changes in BACS and MCCB composite and total SANS scores. Of 21 patients randomized, 18 completed at least 4 weeks of treatment (n=9/group). Pregnenolone was well tolerated. Patients receiving pregnenolone demonstrated significantly greater improvements in SANS scores (mean change=10.38) compared with patients receiving placebo (mean change=2.33), p=0.048. Mean composite changes in BACS and MCCB scores were not significantly different in patients randomized to pregnenolone compared with placebo. However, serum pregnenolone increases predicted BACS composite scores at 8 weeks in the pregnenolone group (r(s)=0.81, p=0.022). Increases in allopregnanolone, a GABAergic pregnenolone metabolite, also predicted BACS composite scores (r(s)=0.74, p=0.046). In addition, baseline pregnenolone (r(s)=-0.76, p=0.037), pregnenolone sulfate (r(s)=-0.83, p=0.015), and allopregnanolone levels (r(s)=-0.83, p=0.015) were inversely correlated with improvements in MCCB composite scores, further supporting a possible role for neurosteroids in cognition. Mean BACS and MCCB composite scores were correlated (r(s)=0.74, p<0.0001). Pregnenolone may be a promising therapeutic agent for negative symptoms and merits further investigation for cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia.
studies.journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology

studies.title: Stability and Reliability of Repeated Plasma Pregnenolone Levels After Oral Pregnenolone Dosing in Individuals with Cocaine Use Disorder: Pilot Findings.
studies.abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs), including cocaine use disorder (CUD), have significant negative health risks and impose a substantial social burden, yet effective treatments are limited. Pregnenolone, a neuroactive steroid precursor, has been shown to reduce alcohol craving and normalize stress biology in individuals with CUD, but its clinical utility has been questioned due to limited data on bioavailability and the stability of blood levels in humans. Thus, this pilot study aimed to determine whether twice-daily oral pregnenolone (PREG) at 300 mg/day and 500 mg/day versus placebo in week two of PREG administration led to stable increased plasma pregnenolone levels in individuals with CUD. Seven treatment-seeking individuals with CUD, enrolled in an eight-week double-blind clinical trial, were randomized to receive placebo (n = 2) or pregnenolone at 300 mg/day (n = 3) or 500 mg/day (n = 2). For the first two weeks of the eight-week trial, participants were admitted to an inpatient Clinical Neuroscience Research Unit for repeated serial sampling of plasma pregnenolone concentrations over a 32.5 h period in week two of their inpatient stay while taking their assigned study drug under observation. Pregnenolone levels showed a significant main effect of the medication group (p = 0.039), with sustained higher levels in the 300 mg (p = 0.018) and 500 mg (p = 0.035) groups compared to placebo, and no significant difference between the two pregnenolone dosing groups. Moreover, correlation analyses showed that after observed study medication dosing on repeated sampling day 1, levels of pregnenolone were highly associated across time, with strong, positive correlations between time of dosing and 2 h (r = 0.80, p = 0.031), 4 h (r = 0.80, p = 0.031), 6 h (r = 0.86, p = 0.013), and 8 h post-dosing (r = 0.97, p < 0.001). These findings from this pilot study suggest that chronic twice-daily/"bis in die" (b.i.d.) oral administration of pregnenolone at both 300 mg/day and 500 mg/day achieved stable and reliable elevated plasma pregnenolone levels over 32.5 h in individuals with CUD, thereby supporting the good bioavailability of pregnenolone in these samples. These data indicate that twice-daily chronic dosing may overcome any potential concerns of poor bioavailability and rapid metabolism of pregnenolone in humans, and support further clinical investigations into pregnenolone's role in the treatment of cocaine use disorders.

studies.title: Pregnenolone Reduces L-Dopa-Induced Dyskinesias in Female Parkinsonian Monkeys.
studies.abstract: Pregnenolone is the first neurosteroid synthesized from cholesterol in the brain. Previous studies showed that it reduces the development of levodopa (L-dopa)-induced dyskinesias (LIDs) in rat models of Parkinson's disease (PD). To examine whether pregnenolone mitigates established LIDs in a non-human primate model. Ovariectomized female macaques, modeling the postmenopausal hormonal status of most women with PD, were lesioned with MPTP and treated with L-dopa to induce LIDs. Pregnenolone was administered subcutaneously (SC) at 6 or 18 mg/kg or orally (36 mg/kg). Pregnenolone reduced established LIDs in MPTP-lesioned monkeys while preserving L-dopa's antiparkinsonian effects. The antidyskinetic effect was dose-dependent, with the greatest reduction observed at 18 mg/kg SC, followed by 6 mg/kg SC, and a lesser effect at 36 mg/kg orally, likely due to first-pass metabolism. Pregnenolone reduces established LIDs in parkinsonian monkeys and may represent a safe, novel therapeutic candidate for dyskinesia treatment in PD. © 2025 The Author(s). studies.title: Impact of Intraventricular Human Adipose-Derived Stem Cells Transplantation with Pregnenolone Treatment on Remyelination of Corpus Callosum in A Rat Model of Mu
studies.abstract:
Objective

Multiple sclerosis (MS) is known as a nerve tissue disorder, which causes demyelination of central nervous system (CNS) fibers. Cell-based treatment is a novel strategy for the treatment of demyelinating diseases such as MS. Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) have neuroprotective and neuroregenerative effects and pregnenolone as a neurosteroid has remarkable roles in neurogenesis. We intend to examine the impact of intraventricular transplantation of human ADSCs and systemic injection of pregnenolone on the remyelination of a rat model cuprizone-induced demyelination.

Materials and methods

This experimental study was performed on 36 male Wistar rats that received a regular diet and a cuprizone diet for 3 weeks for M.S. induction. Through lipoaspirate surgery, human-ADSCs (hADSCs) were obtained from a patient. Six groups of rats (n=6): healthy, MS, sham, pregnenolone injection, ADSCs transplantation, and pregnenolone injection/ADSCs transplantation were included in this study. For assessment of remyelination, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), immunohistochemistry staining, real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were performed.

Results

TEM outcomes revealed an increase in the thickness of the fibers myelin in the treatment groups (P<0.05). We also observed a significant upregulation of MBP, PDGFR-α, and MOG after treatment with hADSCs and pregnenolone compared to other study groups (P<0.001). These results were confirmed by immunostaining analysis. Moreover, there was no significant difference between the ADSCs/pregnenolone group and the control group regarding the level of MBP, A2B5, and MOG proteins in ELISA.

Conclusion

Our data implied that the remyelination and cell recovery were more improved by intraventricular ADSCs transplantation and pregnenolone injection after inducing a rat model of MS.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A natural steroid hormone your body makes; used as a supplement to support mood and cognition.
explanation.what_it_is: Pregnenolone is a steroid hormone—a type of lipid (fat-like) molecule made from cholesterol in your adrenal glands and brain. It sits near the top of the pathway your body uses to manufacture sex hormones and stress hormones. Chemically, it has 21 carbon atoms arranged in a four-ring backbone (the steroid skeleton) with a small side chain, making it highly lipophilic—that is, it dissolves readily in fat and can cross cell membranes easily. People take it as an oral supplement, usually in tablet or capsule form.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Acts on brain receptors and affects steroid hormone pathways; may enhance cell signaling tied to mood and memory.
explanation.how_it_works: Pregnenolone crosses into the brain because of its fat-soluble nature, where it can bind to steroid hormone receptors and also be converted into other neurosteroids (signaling molecules the brain makes). These metabolites, particularly allopregnanolone and DHEA, then interact with GABA and NMDA receptors—key docking sites on brain cells that regulate mood, anxiety, and learning. The mechanism by which it works is not fully established from the human trials alone, but animal work and cell studies suggest it may dampen stress signaling through the HPA axis (a system that controls cortisol release) and enhance memory-linked signaling in the prefrontal cortex. Exactly how these pathways translate to mood and cognition benefits in people remains an open question.
explanation.safety_line: Mostly well-tolerated in short-term trials; long-term safety and effects in key populations not yet tested.
explanation.safety_detail: Trials lasting weeks to months reported few serious adverse events, and dropout rates for side effects were similar to placebo. However, most studies enrolled small numbers of adults with specific psychiatric conditions, and follow-up was brief. Long-term safety, effects in children, pregnancy, kidney or liver disease, and interactions with other hormonal or psychiatric medications have not been adequately studied.
safety_bullets: Pregnancy and nursing: not tested; may influence hormone levels and fetal development—untested in this population.
Children and adolescents: minimal data; one small trial (n=32) in autistic adolescents exists, but safety and long-term effects are unknown.
Hormone-sensitive conditions: effects on breast cancer, prostate cancer, or other steroid-responsive diseases are not established.
Drug interactions: no controlled interaction studies retrieved; combined use with other hormonal agents or psychiatric medications is untested.
explanation.chem_meaning: Pregnenolone's XLogP of 4.2 means it is highly fat-soluble, allowing it to dissolve in body fats and cross cell membranes and the blood–brain barrier readily. This lipophilicity is essential to its ability to enter the brain and interact with steroid receptors there. Its steroid backbone—a rigid four-ring core derived from cholesterol—makes it resistant to breakdown in the stomach and allows it to be absorbed orally.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in people with bipolar depression or schizophrenia (2009–2017, n=11 to 80 per trial) found pregnenolone as an adjunct to antipsychotics reduced depressive or bipolar symptoms more than placebo. A 2017 trial (n=11) in bipolar depression showed changes in a brain protein linked to recovery; a 2017 trial in women with schizophrenia and a 2014 trial (n=80) in bipolar depression both reported mood improvement. Overall, about 91 participants had measurable outcomes across these trials.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Three human RCTs show benefit, but sample sizes are modest (with imprecision across studies) and all enrolled people with severe psychiatric conditions—not healthy or broadly representative populations. Effect sizes appear consistent but are not pooled in a meta-analysis.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two randomized controlled trials in people with schizophrenia (2009 and 2014, n=21 and n=120) tested pregnenolone's effects on cognitive symptoms and impairment. Both reported improvements in cognition (e.g., working memory, processing speed, or negative symptoms like apathy that impair thinking) when pregnenolone was added to antipsychotic drugs, with roughly 141 participants evaluated across the two trials.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Two human RCTs show promise in schizophrenia, but sample sizes remain modest, and both enrolled a single psychiatric condition. No healthy volunteers or dose–response data are available.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Six randomized human trials (2014–2025, n=16 to 80) in people with cocaine use disorder, alcohol use disorder, bipolar disorder, and autism examined pregnenolone's effects on craving, anxiety, and stress markers (HPA axis activity, heart rate, skin conductance). Most found reductions in cue-induced craving and anxiety, and blunted stress hormone responses. One small trial (n=16, 2014) in healthy volunteers examined amygdala (fear-processing brain region) connectivity and found alterations. One animal study in rodents showed similar anxiolytic (anxiety-reducing) effects. Across human studies, roughly 116 participants had measurable anxiety or craving outcomes.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Six human RCTs exist with consistent directional findings, but sample sizes are small and most enroll people with substance use or psychiatric diagnoses. No large, long-term trial in healthy or general populations has been done.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ten randomized human trials (2017–2025) and two animal studies examined pregnenolone in cocaine use disorder, alcohol use disorder, autism with behavioral challenges, and bipolar disorder. Human trials (n=11 to 80) found pregnenolone reduced cue-provoked craving for cocaine and alcohol, decreased reported cocaine use in a small pilot (n=20, 2025), and improved irritable/aggressive behavior in autistic adolescents (n=32, 2020). Animal studies paralleled these findings with reduced drug-seeking behavior. However, the trials vary in design, population, and outcome measures—no meta-analysis confirms consistent effect size.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Ten human RCTs show a pattern of benefit for craving and use reduction, but heterogeneity in populations and methods, modest sample sizes, and lack of a pooled quantitative analysis prevent a strong grade. Grade is held at Moderate pending further review and larger trials.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base consists entirely of human randomized controlled trials—no large animal studies are in the records provided. All trials are recent (2009–2025), with a cluster in 2014 and 2022–2025. Most enrolled 11 to 120 participants with specific psychiatric or substance-use conditions (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, cocaine/alcohol dependence, autism); none enrolled large healthy populations. Durations ranged from acute challenge tests (single doses) to 8–12 weeks. This means evidence is human-sourced and clinically grounded, but limited to specific high-risk populations and short time frames.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not include large trials in healthy adults, adolescents, or geriatric populations. No studies of doses above ~500 mg/day or durations beyond 12 weeks are in the sample. It is unknown whether benefits persist over months or years, whether pregnenolone works for mood or anxiety in the general population, and whether sex, age, or baseline hormone levels modify response. The mechanism—whether pregnenolone itself acts or whether it is converted into other neurosteroids—remains incompletely characterized in human studies.

appraisal.headline: All four outcomes rest on small, non-pooled RCTs (median sample 21–80 per study) with no meta-analysis confirming consistency; a single large negative trial or replication failure could overturn the grade.

concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes, 40–60% of trials do not report sample size in the retrieved records. Mood/depression: 1 of 3 studies missing n. Cognition: 0 of 2 missing n. Stress/anxiety: 4 of 7 missing n. Substance use disorder: 7 of 12 missing n. This prevents verification of true total participant exposure and allows high-risk small studies to be invisible in summaries.

concerns.issue: No pooled effect estimates despite multiple trials
concerns.detail: The engine reports 'none extractable' for all four outcomes, meaning no meta-analysis or systematic quantitative synthesis exists. The stress/anxiety outcome explicitly flags 'Inconsistency: several studies exist but no pooled analysis confirms they agree.' With 3–10 RCTs per outcome, the absence of a pooled result suggests either heterogeneity too large to combine, unpublished protocols, or selective reporting of compatible studies.

concerns.issue: Severe imprecision with unstable effect estimates
concerns.detail: The engine flags imprecision for mood (91 participants in 2 of 3 studies), cognition (141 participants in 2 of 2 studies), and stress/anxiety (116 participants in 3 of 7 studies). With median sample sizes of 20–80, confidence intervals are likely wide and asymmetric. The smallest study had n=11; a single outlier outcome in a trial of this size could shift the nominal direction of effect.

concerns.issue: Narrow, overlapping, and specialized study populations
concerns.detail: The clinical populations are highly selected: bipolar depression, schizophrenia, cocaine/alcohol use disorder, and autism spectrum disorder. Only one study explicitly targets cognition in a general population (n=21, 2009). Mood outcomes come almost entirely from bipolar/psychotic samples. Stress/anxiety outcomes conflate cocaine craving, alcohol craving, and amygdala connectivity—conceptually related but not identical constructs. Generalizability to typical users (e.g., healthy adults or non-psychotic mood states) is not evidenced.

concerns.issue: Recent studies cluster on substance use craving; earlier studies on psychosis
concerns.detail: Mood and cognition studies span 2009–2017 with no new data since 2017. Stress/anxiety and substance use disorder studies show a jump to 2022–2025, clustering on cocaine and alcohol craving reduction. This temporal and thematic shift raises the question whether recent craving outcomes are driving the Moderate grade upward, while older outcomes on mood/cognition remain underpowered and unchanged. No study bridges both old and new indication domains.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Pregnenolone is proposed to act as a neurosteroid precursor modulating GABA and glutamate signaling, amygdala connectivity, and HPA axis function. The jump from putative neurochemical activity to clinical mood, cognition, and craving reduction is plausible at the level of known neurobiology, but the retrieved studies do not report mechanistic confirmation (e.g., dose-response on HPA axis correlating with symptom change, or biomarker validation). The cognition and craving outcomes rely on behavioral measurement alone; no studies show target engagement (e.g., pregnenolone levels, receptor occupancy, or biomarker change in responders vs. non-responders).
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that these are small, geographically and institutionally clustered trials (most from the same research group at a single medical center, based on study titles and years), none has been independently replicated at scale, and no meta-analysis confirms effect direction or magnitude. The recent craving studies (2022–2025) may reflect publication bias: small, positive early-phase trials in addiction are more likely to be submitted and accepted, while null or negative trials go unpublished. The absence of a pooled estimate despite 3–10 RCTs per outcome is itself evidence of either heterogeneity or selective reporting.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A multi-center, pre-registered RCT of pregnenolone vs. placebo in ≥200 participants with a single, well-defined outcome (e.g., depressive symptom reduction in bipolar disorder, or cognitive performance in schizophrenia) with intent-to-treat analysis and pre-specified primary endpoint would provide direct power to resolve imprecision. A meta-analysis pooling effect sizes from existing RCTs with subgroup analysis by indication (mood vs. cognition vs. craving) and sensitivity analysis by study size would immediately clarify whether inconsistency is real or apparent.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una hormona esteroide natural que tu cuerpo produce; utilizada como suplemento para apoyar el estado de ánimo y la cognición.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La pregnenolona es una hormona esteroide—un tipo de molécula lipídica (similar a la grasa) sintetizada a partir del colesterol en tus glándulas adrenales y cerebro. Se sitúa cerca de la parte superior de la vía que tu cuerpo utiliza para fabricar hormonas sexuales y hormonas del estrés. Químicamente, tiene 21 átomos de carbono organizados en un esqueleto de cuatro anillos (el esqueleto esteroide) con una pequeña cadena lateral, lo que la hace altamente lipófila—es decir, se disuelve fácilmente en grasa y puede atravesar las membranas celulares con facilidad. Las personas la toman como suplemento oral, generalmente en forma de tableta o cápsula.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Actúa en receptores cerebrales y afecta las vías de hormonas esteroides; puede mejorar la señalización celular vinculada al estado de ánimo y la memoria.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La pregnenolona cruza hacia el cerebro debido a su naturaleza soluble en grasa, donde puede unirse a receptores de hormonas esteroides y también ser convertida en otros neuroesteroides (moléculas de señalización que el cerebro produce). Estos metabolitos, particularmente la alopreganolona y DHEA, luego interactúan con receptores GABA y NMDA—sitios de acoplamiento clave en las células cerebrales que regulan el estado de ánimo, la ansiedad y el aprendizaje. El mecanismo por el cual actúa no está completamente establecido a partir de los ensayos en humanos únicamente, pero el trabajo en animales y los estudios celulares sugieren que puede disminuir la señalización del estrés a través del eje HPA (un sistema que controla la liberación de cortisol) y mejorar la señalización vinculada a la memoria en la corteza prefrontal. La forma exacta en que estas vías se traducen en beneficios del estado de ánimo y la cognición en las personas sigue siendo una pregunta abierta.
explanation_es.safety_line: Generalmente bien tolerada en ensayos a corto plazo; la seguridad a largo plazo y los efectos en poblaciones clave aún no han sido probados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos que duraron semanas a meses reportaron pocos eventos adversos graves, y las tasas de abandonos por efectos secundarios fueron similares al placebo. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios incluyeron números pequeños de adultos con condiciones psiquiátricas específicas, y el seguimiento fue breve. La seguridad a largo plazo, los efectos en niños, el embarazo, la enfermedad renal o hepática, y las interacciones con otros medicamentos hormonales o psiquiátricos no han sido adecuadamente estudiados.
safety_bullets: Embarazo y lactancia: no probado; puede influir en los niveles de hormonas y el desarrollo fetal—no probado en esta población.
Niños y adolescentes: datos mínimos; existe un ensayo pequeño (n=32) en adolescentes autistas, pero la seguridad y los efectos a largo plazo son desconocidos.
Condiciones sensibles a hormonas: los efectos en el cáncer de mama, cáncer de próstata u otras enfermedades sensibles a esteroides no están establecidos.
Interacciones farmacológicas: no se encontraron estudios de interacción controlados; el uso combinado con otros agentes hormonales o medicamentos psiquiátricos no ha sido probado.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: El XLogP de 4.2 de la pregnenolona significa que es altamente soluble en grasa, lo que le permite disolverse en las grasas corporales y atravesar fácilmente las membranas celulares y la barrera hematoencefálica. Esta lipofilicidad es esencial para su capacidad de entrar en el cerebro e interactuar con receptores esteroides allí. Su esqueleto esteroide—un núcleo rígido de cuatro anillos derivado del colesterol—la hace resistente a la descomposición en el estómago y le permite ser absorbida oralmente.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos aleatorizados, doble ciego y controlados con placebo en personas con depresión bipolar o esquizofrenia (2009–2017, n=11 a 80 por ensayo) encontraron que la pregnenolona como adyuvante a antipsicóticos redujo los síntomas depresivos o bipolares más que el placebo. Un ensayo de 2017 (n=11) en depresión bipolar mostró cambios en una proteína cerebral vinculada a la recuperación; un ensayo de 2017 en mujeres con esquizofrenia y un ensayo de 2014 (n=80) en depresión bipolar ambos reportaron mejoría del estado de ánimo. En total, aproximadamente 91 participantes tuvieron resultados medibles en estos ensayos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos muestran beneficio, pero los tamaños de muestra son modestos (con imprecisión entre estudios) y todos incluyeron personas con condiciones psiquiátricas graves—no poblaciones sanas o ampliamente representativas. Los tamaños del efecto parecen consistentes pero no están agrupados en un metanálisis.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos ensayos controlados aleatorizados en personas con esquizofrenia (2009 y 2014, n=21 y n=120) probaron los efectos de la pregnenolona en los síntomas cognitivos y el deterioro. Ambos reportaron mejoras en la cognición (p. ej., memoria de trabajo, velocidad de procesamiento, o síntomas negativos como la apatía que afecta el pensamiento) cuando la pregnenolona se agregó a medicamentos antipsicóticos, con aproximadamente 141 participantes evaluados en los dos ensayos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Dos ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos muestran promesa en esquizofrenia, pero los tamaños de muestra siguen siendo modestos, y ambos incluyeron una única condición psiquiátrica. No hay datos disponibles de voluntarios sanos ni respuesta a dosis.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seis ensayos aleatorizados en humanos (2014–2025, n=16 a 80) en personas con trastorno por consumo de cocaína, trastorno por consumo de alcohol, trastorno bipolar y autismo examinaron los efectos de la pregnenolona en el craving, la ansiedad y los marcadores de estrés (actividad del eje HPA, frecuencia cardíaca, conductancia de la piel). La mayoría encontró reducciones en el craving inducido por señales y la ansiedad, y respuestas de hormonas de estrés atenuadas. Un ensayo pequeño (n=16, 2014) en voluntarios sanos examinó la conectividad de la amígdala (región cerebral de procesamiento del miedo) y encontró alteraciones. Un estudio en animales en roedores mostró efectos ansiolíticos similares (reductores de la ansiedad). En los estudios en humanos, aproximadamente 116 participantes tuvieron resultados medibles de ansiedad o craving.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Seis ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos existen con hallazgos direccionales consistentes, pero los tamaños de muestra son pequeños y la mayoría incluye personas con diagnósticos de abuso de sustancias o psiquiátricos. Ningún ensayo grande a largo plazo en poblaciones sanas o generales ha sido realizado.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Diez ensayos aleatorizados en humanos (2017–2025) y dos estudios en animales examinaron la pregnenolona en trastorno por consumo de cocaína, trastorno por consumo de alcohol, autismo con desafíos de comportamiento, y trastorno bipolar. Los ensayos en humanos (n=11 a 80) encontraron que la pregnenolona redujo el craving provocado por señales para cocaína y alcohol, disminuyó el uso reportado de cocaína en un piloto pequeño (n=20, 2025), y mejoró el comportamiento irritable/agresivo en adolescentes autistas (n=32, 2020). Los estudios en animales respaldaron estos hallazgos con comportamiento de búsqueda de drogas reducido. Sin embargo, los ensayos varían en diseño, población y medidas de resultado—ningún metanálisis confirma un tamaño de efecto consistente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Diez ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos muestran un patrón de beneficio para la reducción del craving y el uso, pero la heterogeneidad en poblaciones y métodos, tamaños de muestra modestos, y la falta de un análisis cuantitativo agrupado previenen una calificación fuerte. La calificación se mantiene en Moderada pendiente de revisión adicional y ensayos más grandes.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia consiste enteramente en ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos—no hay estudios en animales grandes en los registros proporcionados. Todos los ensayos son recientes (2009–2025), con un grupo en 2014 y 2022–2025. La mayoría incluyó 11 a 120 participantes con condiciones psiquiátricas o de abuso de sustancias específicas (esquizofrenia, trastorno bipolar, dependencia de cocaína/alcohol, autismo); ninguno incluyó poblaciones sanas grandes. Las duraciones variaron desde pruebas de desafío agudo (dosis únicas) hasta 8–12 semanas. Esto significa que la evidencia está basada en humanos y clínicamente fundamentada, pero limitada a poblaciones específicas de alto riesgo y marcos de tiempo breves.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no incluyen ensayos grandes en adultos sanos, adolescentes o poblaciones geriátricas. No hay estudios de dosis superiores a ~500 mg/día o duraciones superiores a 12 semanas en la muestra. Se desconoce si los beneficios persisten durante meses o años, si la pregnenolona funciona para el estado de ánimo o la ansiedad en la población general, y si el sexo, la edad o los niveles basales de hormonas modifican la respuesta. El mecanismo—si la pregnenolona misma actúa o si es convertida en otros neuroesteroides—sigue siendo incompletamente caracterizado en estudios en humanos.

appraisal_es.headline: Los cuatro resultados se basan en ensayos controlados aleatorizados pequeños y no agrupados (mediana de muestra 21–80 por estudio) sin metanálisis que confirme consistencia; un único ensayo negativo grande o fallo de replicación podría invertir la calificación.

concerns.issue: Notificación sistemática insuficiente de tamaños de muestra
concerns.detail: En los cuatro resultados, 40–60% de los ensayos no reportan el tamaño de muestra en los registros recuperados. Humor/depresión: 1 de 3 estudios sin n. Cognición: 0 de 2 sin n. Estrés/ansiedad: 4 de 7 sin n. Trastorno por uso de sustancias: 7 de 12 sin n. Esto impide la verificación de la verdadera exposición total de participantes y permite que estudios pequeños de alto riesgo sean invisibles en los resúmenes.

concerns.issue: Sin estimaciones de efecto agrupado a pesar de múltiples ensayos
concerns.detail: El motor reporta 'ninguno extraíble' para los cuatro resultados, lo que significa que no existe metanálisis ni síntesis cuantitativa sistemática. El resultado de estrés/ansiedad explícitamente señala 'Inconsistencia: existen varios estudios pero ningún análisis agrupado confirma que estén de acuerdo.' Con 3–10 ensayos controlados aleatorizados por resultado, la ausencia de un resultado agrupado sugiere heterogeneidad demasiado grande para combinar, protocolos no publicados, o reporte selectivo de estudios compatibles.

concerns.issue: Imprecisión severa con estimaciones de efecto inestables
concerns.detail: El motor señala imprecisión para humor (91 participantes en 2 de 3 estudios), cognición (141 participantes en 2 de 2 estudios), y estrés/ansiedad (116 participantes en 3 de 7 estudios). Con tamaños de muestra medianos de 20–80, los intervalos de confianza probablemente sean amplios y asimétricos. El estudio más pequeño tuvo n=11; un resultado atípico único en un ensayo de este tamaño podría cambiar la dirección nominal del efecto.

concerns.issue: Poblaciones de estudio estrechas, superpuestas y especializadas
concerns.detail: Las poblaciones clínicas son altamente seleccionadas: depresión bipolar, esquizofrenia, trastorno por uso de cocaína/alcohol, y trastorno del espectro autista. Solo un estudio apunta explícitamente a la cognición en población general (n=21, 2009). Los resultados de humor provienen casi enteramente de muestras bipolares/psicóticas. Los resultados de estrés/ansiedad confunden el craving de cocaína, el craving de alcohol, y la conectividad amigdalina—constructos conceptualmente relacionados pero no idénticos. La generalizabilidad a usuarios típicos (p. ej., adultos sanos o estados de humor no psicóticos) no está evidenciada.

concerns.issue: Estudios recientes agrupados en craving por sustancias; estudios anteriores en psicosis
concerns.detail: Los estudios de humor y cognición abarcan 2009–2017 sin datos nuevos desde 2017. Los estudios de estrés/ansiedad y trastorno por uso de sustancias muestran un salto a 2022–2025, agrupados en reducción de craving de cocaína y alcohol. Este cambio temporal y temático plantea la pregunta de si los resultados de craving recientes están impulsando la calificación Moderada hacia arriba, mientras que los resultados anteriores de humor/cognición permanecen insuficientemente potenciados e inalterados. Ningún estudio une ambos dominios de indicación antiguos y nuevos.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Se propone que la pregnenolona actúe como precursor de neuroesteroide modulando la señalización GABA y glutamato, la conectividad amigdalina, y la función del eje HPA. El salto de la actividad neuroquímica propuesta a la reducción clínica de humor, cognición y craving es plausible a nivel de la neurobiología conocida, pero los estudios recuperados no reportan confirmación mecanicista (p. ej., respuesta a la dosis en el eje HPA correlacionada con cambio de síntomas, o validación de biomarcador). Los resultados de cognición y craving se basan únicamente en medición conductual; ningún estudio muestra compromiso del objetivo (p. ej., niveles de pregnenolona, ocupancia de receptor, o cambio de biomarcador en respondedores versus no-respondedores).
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico notaría que estos son ensayos pequeños, geográfica e institucionalmente agrupados (la mayoría del mismo grupo de investigación en un único centro médico, basado en títulos de estudios y años), ninguno ha sido replicado de forma independiente a escala, y ningún metanálisis confirma la dirección o magnitud del efecto. Los estudios de craving recientes (2022–2025) pueden reflejar sesgo de publicación: ensayos pequeños y positivos en fases tempranas en adicción son más propensos a ser enviados y aceptados, mientras que ensayos nulos o negativos quedan sin publicar. La ausencia de una estimación agrupada a pesar de 3–10 ensayos controlados aleatorizados por resultado es en sí misma evidencia de heterogeneidad o reporte selectivo.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo controlado aleatorizado multicéntrico, preregistrado de pregnenolona versus placebo en ≥200 participantes con un resultado único y bien definido (p. ej., reducción de síntomas depresivos en trastorno bipolar, o desempeño cognitivo en esquizofrenia) con análisis por intención de tratar y punto final primario preespecificado proporcionaría potencia directa para resolver la imprecisión. Un metanálisis agrupando tamaños de efecto de ensayos controlados aleatorizados existentes con análisis de subgrupo por indicación (humor versus cognición versus craving) y análisis de sensibilidad por tamaño de estudio aclararía inmediatamente si la inconsistencia es real o aparente.
